title: Listing of Color Additives Exempt From Certification; Gardenia (Genipin) Blue; Confirmation of Effective Date
summary:
Two notable updates from Washington: a natural blue color is now cleared for wider use in foods and drinks in the United States, and a past decision to apply U.S. sanctions to Iran’s financial sector has been formally published.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration confirmed that “gardenia (genipin) blue” can be used as a color in sports drinks, flavored or enhanced waters, fruit drinks and ades, ready-to-drink teas, and hard and soft candies. The agency had previously opened the door to this ingredient and received no objections, so the rule took effect on August 29, 2025. For food and beverage makers, this adds a plant-derived option to achieve blue shades, which could help brands that are leaning into simpler labels and natural colors. Suppliers of natural ingredients and product developers may see new demand and formulation flexibility. On the flip side, companies that rely on synthetic blue dyes could face more competition, and smaller manufacturers may need to check sourcing and specs carefully to stay compliant, especially after the agency clarified the methanol specification earlier this summer.

Separately, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control published its determination that U.S. sanctions apply to Iran’s financial sector, a step originally taken on October 8, 2020. While this does not change current practice, it underscores that U.S. persons and firms face restrictions when dealing with Iranian financial institutions. Compliance teams and risk managers gain clarity in the public record, while the burden and exposure increase for any business with ties to that sector. The most direct negative impact remains on Iran’s financial system and entities that transact with it, and there can be knock-on effects for humanitarian trade if channels are not clearly safeguarded.

Bottom line: food companies get a new natural blue to work with, and the sanctions landscape remains firm for Iran’s financial sector. Both actions offer regulatory certainty, but they also ask businesses to adjust—whether in product formulations or in compliance and due diligence.
